TO:  The Honorable Mayor and City Council
FROM:  Martha Garcia, Director of Finance
SUBJECT:  Resolutions of the Los Angeles County Treasury Pool; Local Agency
  Investment Fund; and California Department of Tax and Fee
  Administration

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  1. Adopting Resolutions to update authoritative titles for the Los Angeles County
  Investment Pool (County), Local Agency Investment Fund (LAIF), and California
  Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA); and
  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
On the November 8, 2022, the voters of Monterey Park passed Measure MP, a ¾ cent
transactions and use (sales) tax to provide funding for local city services. The CDTFA
Resolution seeks Council’s authorization to designate, in writing, the officer(s),
employee(s), and any other person(s) authorized to examine transactions and use tax
records as required by the CDTFA.

On December 7, 2022, a new Monterey Park City Treasurer took office. The County
and LAIF Resolutions seek Council authorization to designate, in writing, the officer(s),
employee(s), and any other person(s) authorized to deposit, withdraw, and invest in
such funds.

BACKGROUND:
The County, LAIF and the CDTFA require written City Council approval to administer
and/or examine City funds. The three draft Resolutions attached meet the requirements
of each agency.

Staff is requesting adopting the three Resolutions to allow the identified staff and City
Treasurer to manage and monitor City funds.

FISCAL IMPACT:
No fiscal impact.

A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING AND REQUESTING THE INVESTMENT OF
EXCESS FUNDS IN THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY TREASURY POOL

THE CITY COUNCIL DOES RESOLVE AS FOLLOWS:

SECTION 1: The City Council finds as follows:

  A.  Government Code § 53684 allows local agencies located within the
  County of Los Angeles (the "County") to deposit excess funds in the Los
  Angeles County Treasury Pool for the purpose of investment by the
  Treasurer and Tax Collector of the County (the "Treasurer);

  B.  The City of Monterey Park has been depositing idle monies with Los
  Angeles County Treasury for the purpose of investing since August
  2013;

  C.  It is desirable for the City to deposit from time to time idle funds in the
  County Treasury Pool for the purpose of investment pursuant to
  Government Code §§ 53601 and 53635;

  D.  The City will inform the Treasurer if and to the extent any of the City of
  Monterey Park's funds deposited in the County Treasury Pool pursuant
  to this Resolution are proceeds of the issuance of bonds, certificates of
  participation, notes or other evidences of indebtedness ("Bond
  Proceeds"). If the Bond Proceeds are restricted by a certificate of the
  City relating to compliance with federal tax requirement ("Nonarbitrage
  Certificate"), the City agrees to provide the Nonarbitrage Certificate to
  the Treasurer so that the Treasurer can provide the market value of the
  Bond Proceeds as of the rebate calculation dates as provided in the
  Nonarbitrage Certificate. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the County
  takes no responsibility and the City is solely responsible for compliance
  with the terms and conditions of the Nonarbitrage Certificates and of any
  federal tax requirements that may apply to the Bond issuance. The City
  will review bond documents to determine if funds can be deposited into
  the County Treasury Pool; and

  E.  The City agrees that the County may calculate the average daily balance
  of participants in the County Treasury Pool and may allocate monthly
  interest payments thereon pursuant to any reasonable method
  established by the County and consistently applied. The City agrees to
  reimburse to the County Treasury Pool any amounts disbursed to the
  City in error promptly upon the discovery of such error or upon the
  request of the Treasurer.

SECTION 2: Authority. The City Manager, Assistant City Manager, City Treasurer,

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  MONTEREY PARK AUTHORIZING EXAMINATION OF
  SALES OR TRANSACTIONS AND USE TAXES RECORDS

WHEREAS, pursuant to Ordinance Numbers 1360 and 2225 of the City of Monterey
Park (“City”), and Revenue and Taxation Code section 7270, the City entered into a
contract with the California Department of Tax and Fee Administration (“Department”) to
perform all functions incident to the administration and collection of transactions and
use taxes; and

WHEREAS, the City Council deems it desirable and necessary for authorized officers,
employees and representatives of the City to examine confidential sales or transactions
and use tax records of the Department pertaining to transactions and use taxes
collected by the Department for the City pursuant to that contract; and

WHEREAS, Section 7056 of the California Revenue and Taxation Code sets forth
certain requirements and conditions for the disclosure of Department records, and
Section 7056.5 of the California Revenue and Taxation Code establishes criminal
penalties for the unlawful disclosure of information contained in, or derived from, the
sales or transactions and use tax records of the Department;

NOW, THEREFORE, THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF MONTEREY PARK
HEREBY RESOLVES AS FOLLOWS:

SECTION 1: That the City Manager, City Attorney, Assistant City Manager, Director of
Finance and Finance Manager or other officer or employee of the City designated in
writing by the City Manager to the California Department of Tax and Fee Administration
is hereby appointed to represent the City with authority to examine sales or transactions
and use tax records of the Department pertaining to transactions and use taxes
collected for the City by the Department pursuant to the contract between the City and
the Department.

SECTION 2: The information obtained by examination of Department records shall be
used only for purposes related to the collection of City transactions and use taxes by the
Department pursuant to that contract, and for purposes related to the following
governmental functions of the City:

  (a) Budget planning and revenue management

  (b) Transportation planning

  (c) Community and economic development

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
In 2013, the City Council added Chapter 2.82 to the Monterey Park Municipal Code
("MPMC") restructuring the establishment of the Commissions, Boards and Committees,
collectively "Commissions," and redefines the appointment procedures. In accordance
with the MPMC, each council member appoints his/her respective representative(s) to the
9 commissions to serve a maximum of two 4-year terms. If an individual separates from
serving on a board or commission because the individual has completed serving terms,
such person cannot be reappointed to the same board or commission for at least twelve
consecutive months unless authorized by City Council to extend their term. Commissions
term is automatically rolled over unless otherwise directed by council members.

BACKGROUND:
Each council member may appoint 1 member to Business Improvement District Advisory
Committee, Design Review Board, Economic Development Advisory Commission,
Environmental Commission, Planning Commission, Recreation and Parks Commission,
and Traffic Commission; and 2 members to the Commission on Aging and Community
Participation Commission.  Certain commissions may have certain background
requirements to qualify. Each commissioner serves at the pleasure of the appointing
council member.

Attached to the staff report is MPMC § 2.82, Resolution No. 11589, a blank Application
for Civic Service and a spreadsheet listing current commissioners for each individual
council member. Council members can review, confirm appointments, extend terms,
and/or make new selections at a subsequence council meeting or by contacting the City
Clerk’s office. Commissioners will be required to submit an application, have their
fingerprinting completed, and/or complete a residency verification form upon
appointment.

  RECOMMENDATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  (1)  Adopting a resolution amending Resolution Nos. 12155 and 12195

  Responsibilities; and
  (2)  Take such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:

On September 16, 2020, the City Council amended Resolution No. 12155 and adopted
Resolution No. 12195 memorializing actions taken by City Council and establishing
procedures for City Council reorganization and rotating mayoral responsibilities. The draft
resolution amends Resolution Nos. 12155 and 12195 to clarify the rotation order and set
subsequent appointments of mayor and mayor pro tempore. No other changes are
proposed.

BACKGROUND:

In 1982, the City Council established a policy giving each City Councilmember an
opportunity to be Mayor at least once during their term. That policy established a nine
month and two week mayoral term for each Councilmember.

In 1994, the City Council adopted Resolution No. 9921 which temporarily established an
11 month and two week mayoral term until January 1999. This was implemented in order
to accommodate the City’s change in election dates caused by California law. After
January 1999, the mayor rotation reverted to the original nine month and two week term
established in 1982.

In 2012, the City Council adopted Resolution No. 11507. That Resolution established a
mayoral term which was 41 weeks. Section 6 of Resolution No. 11507 provides that “[b]y
affirmative vote of not less than four members of the Council, the provisions of this
resolution may be suspended, and any member of the Council may be appointed to the
position of Mayor or Mayor Pro Tempore for a fixed or indeterminate term or terms.”

  The Council of the City of Monterey Park does resolve as follows:

SECTION 1: Findings. The City Council finds as follows:

  A.  In 1982, the City Council established a policy for mayoral rotation that
  gave each member of the City Council an opportunity to be Mayor at least
  once during their term. Resolution No. 8584 created a nine month and two
  week mayoral term for each Councilmember.

  B.  In 1994, the City Council adopted Resolution No. 9921 which temporarily
  established an 11 month and two week mayoral term until January 1999.
  This was implemented in order to accommodate the City’s change in
  election dates caused by California law. After January 1999, the mayor
  rotation reverted to the nine month and two week term established by
  Resolution No. 8584.

  C.  In 2012, the City Council adopted Resolution No. 11507. That Resolution
  established a mayoral term which was 41 weeks. It further amended
  Resolution Nos. 8585 and 9921 to conform to Resolution No. 11507.

  D.  Section 6 of Resolution No. 11507 provides that “[b]y affirmative vote of
  not less than four members of the Council, the provisions of this resolution
  may be suspended, and any member of the Council may be appointed to
  the position of Mayor or Mayor Pro Tempore for a fixed or indeterminate
  term or terms.”

  E.  On May 31, 2019, the City’s former at-large election system for City
  Council switched to district elections. In accordance with Monterey Park
  Municipal Code (“MPMC”) §§ 2.04.060 to 2.04.090, the City’s first district-
  based election occurred on March 3, 2020 for Districts 2, 3, and 4.

  F.  Three individuals were elected to the City Council on March 3, 2020.
  Based upon the policy of Resolution No. 8584, individuals with the highest
  number of votes would be ranked for the order of mayoral appointment,
  i.e., the person with the highest number of votes would be ranked first.

  G.  In 2020, the City Council adopted Resolution Nos. 12155 (May 6, 2020)
  and 12195 (September 16, 2020). These Resolutions temporarily
  amended the rotation schedule based upon the COVID-19 Pandemic
  emergency and at the request of Fred Sornoso, representing District 3.

by conducting routine inspections and cleaning to avoid flooding issues. Once the CPS

on the state’s formula, the City is currently at 98.2% and should be at 99% to meet the
state mandate of trash reduction. All City owned catch basins are currently fitted with a
Connector Pipe Screen retrofit device. The Connector Pipe Screen (CPS) units prevent
trash and debris from entering the storm drain system during dry weather and moderate
storm flows by keeping the trash and debris inside the catch basin. In order to meet 99%
trash reduction target, the City can also retrofit LA County-owned catch basins located
within the City with CPS devices.

CPS units in 130 county-owned catch basins. The work included cleaning of the existing
catch basins and installing CPS units following LA County standards. United Storm Water
CPS Unit specifications are one of the few approved by LA County. Staff recommends
amending United Storm Water, Inc.’s agreement, for the installation of CPS Units at an
additional 100 catch basins. The proposed cost for the additional work will use the same
unit prices presented in United Storm Water, Inc.’s previous bid submitted on May 2022.

3-H.  AMENDMENT TO UNITED STORM WATER INC. AGREEMENT 2309-A, AND
  AWARD OF CONTRACT FOR CATCH BASIN MAINTENANCE

  On June 2022, City Council approved a Public Works contract with United Storm
  Water, Inc., to install Connector Pipe Screen (CPS) units at 130 catch basin
  locations throughout the City. The Public Works contract was for a total amount of
  $99,450, and contingency up to $9,945 or 10% of the contract amount. To reach
  the City’s 99% trash discharge reduction goal, the City’s Stormwater Program
  consultant, John L. Hunter determined that retrofitting an additional 100 catch
  basins will be required. Staff recommends amending the current agreement with
  United Storm Water for the installation of an additional 100 CPS units, increasing
  the approved contract amount from $109,395 to $199,395.

  Furthermore, the City is currently responsible for maintaining all City owned catch
  basins by conducting routine inspections and cleaning to avoid flooding issues.
  Once the CPS units are installed, the City will also be responsible for maintaining
  the retrofit device and county-owned catch basin per the County of Los Angeles
  Maintenance Standards. Staff recommends the award of a maintenance contract
  to United Storm Water for the inspection and cleaning of retrofitted County owned
  catch basins and all City owned catch basins. The proposed agreement would be
  for three years with the option to extend for two one-year terms. The estimated
  term cost for services is $60,000 per year, with annual CPI increases.

  CEQA (California Environmental Quality Act)
  Since the proposed work is a minor alteration to an existing public facility, this
  project is Class 1 Categorically Exempt pursuant to the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA).

  Action Taken: The City Council authorized the City Manager to execute the First
  Amendment, in a form approved by the City Attorney, to Agreement No. 2309-A
  with United Storm Water, Inc., to retrofit an additional 100 catch basins with
  Connector Pipe Screens in the amount of $90,000 including labor and 15%
  contingency; and authorized the City Manager to execute a three-year
  Maintenance Agreement with an option to extend for an additional two one-year
  terms, in a form approved by the City Attorney, with United Storm Water, Inc, in an
  amount of $60,000 per year with annual CPI increases, for the maintenance of all
  City-owned catch basins and retrofitted County owned catch basins with
  Connector Pipe Screen (CPS) Units on Consent Calendar.
